 Advertisement Kale chips recalled nationwide due to potential thallium contamination
 Advertisement Updated: 2:51 PM CST Nov 4, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Brian Wiechert Digital Content Manager Kale chips recalled nationwide due to potential thallium contamination
 Updated: 2:51 PM CST Nov 4, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Brian Wiechert Digital Content Manager Kale chips have been recalled nationwide over potential thallium contamination, which officials warn could cause nerve damage or hair loss.
 Snack Right Super Foods is recalling certain bags of Brad’s kale chips because they may contain the naturally occurring metal. 
 Advertisement Related video above | Recalls explained: How to stay ahead of recalls 
 The affected products were distributed nationwide from October through December 2025, officials with the Food and Drug Administration announced Tuesday.
 The recall covers specific lots of Brad’s Crunchy Kale in Original, Cheeze It Up and Radical Ranch flavors, plus Brad’s Veggie Chips Kale. 
 The bags are 2 or 3 ounces, and the affected lots have best-by dates from Dec. 21, 2026, through Feb. 17, 2027. You can check the lot numbers and UPCs in the company’s recall notice .
 Thallium can cause serious health problems at high levels of exposure, including stomach and intestinal illness, nerve damage and hair loss. 
 The company says the metal was not introduced during manufacturing. 
 Rather, kale can take up elements from soil, and drying the kale removes water and concentrates elements already present.
 The recall follows testing by the FDA and an earlier investigation by California health officials, who found elevated thallium in samples of several Brad’s products.
 If you have an affected bag, stop eating it and throw it away. The company says it is not offering refunds, and asks consumers not to return the product to the store. If you think you have had a health effect after eating the chips, contact a health care provider.
